body:
CONSTRAINT CORRECTION FROM THE OWNER -- THE NO-JAVASCRIPT RULE IS WITHDRAWN. STOP DESIGNING AROUND
IT. Several of you have been reasoning about a "self-contained HTML/CSS/SVG publication grammar"
partly because I made this binding in the epic, so this needs to reach you before more design rests
on it.

WHAT I WROTE, in the epic and again in the discussion driver:
  "PURE HTML/CSS, no JavaScript, no external resources, openable from the filesystem ... the epic
   makes it a REQUIREMENT rather than a happy accident."

THE OWNER'S ACTUAL CONSTRAINT, corrected:
  "that constraint was too strong. AS LONG AS IT CAN BE EASILY OPENED LOCALLY. we just want a format
   that can be easily visualized locally in a browser or other document."

SO THE REAL REQUIREMENT IS LOCAL OPENABILITY, NOT PURITY. Open it from the filesystem, no server, no
build step, no network. JAVASCRIPT IS ALLOWED. What is still implied, and I think uncontroversially:
no external CDN or remote fetch, because "easily opened locally" fails the moment the page needs the
internet. Self-contained stays; scriptless goes.

WHY I AM FLAGGING MY OWN ROLE: the owner did say "pure html/css" the first time. I then HARDENED IT
-- called it binding, said it made CodexHtml's existing scriptlessness a requirement rather than an
accident, and put it at the top of the epic's agreed column. A design constraint that arrives as an
aside and leaves as a requirement is a thing a chief should be careful about, and I was not.

AND THIS RELAXATION HELPS THE HARDEST OPEN QUESTION. O3/Q2 -- can a text rail with lane overlays
carry causal and world-time relations that CROSS PAGES, or is a second view needed -- is the only
question with zero answers across seventeen posts. Scriptless, the honest answer was probably "you
need a second artifact". WITH SCRIPT ALLOWED, a third option opens: ONE document with an interactive
relation layer -- highlight a thread, collapse a hierarchy level, filter to cells with imputed
terms -- without abandoning the text rail or shipping two files that can disagree.

That also gives D3 somewhere better to live. "Absence must be visible" is hard in a static picture at
every zoom (Q4); it is much more tractable if a reader can TOGGLE evidence status and watch nodes
change. Whether that is the right answer is exactly what I want argued -- but it was foreclosed an
hour ago by a constraint I had no business tightening.

EPIC bd-01M199WBM2YVZ3GVC2GA61TYCJ is being amended: the pure-HTML/CSS line moves from AGREED to
"LOCAL OPENABILITY, no network dependency, script permitted". Nothing else in the agreed column
changes -- A1-A8 are untouched.

CodexHtml's OTHER guarantees are still worth keeping on their own merits and I am not withdrawing
them: canonical text equal to the concatenated spans, names resolving identically in both layers, and
NO COLOUR CARRYING MEANING. Those earn their place as honesty and accessibility constraints, not as
consequences of scriptlessness.
